To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inlet-air temperature was the most critical process variables for all response variables studied.

the inlet-air temperature was the most important process variable for the three response variables considered, namely, the drug release rate from the “untained” and “thermal-treated” tablets and the hardness of the “untreated coated tablets.

the rate of drug release and the microindentations hardness of the applied coat were affected by inlet-air temperature, percent solids content of the polymeric coating dispersion, and the spray rate of the coating polymeric solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation and optimization of the coating process variables in a fluid-bed process for a plasticized aqueos ethylcellullose dispersion.
the evaluation of the effect of coating process variables on the performance characteristics (rate of drug release and microindentation) of the applied polyethylcellulose coat.
the development of a mathematical model for the optimization of selected coating process variables in order to achieve the desired performance characteristics of tablets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of drug release and the microindentability of the applied polymer coat are dependent upon the process variables studied.

the inlet-air temperature and the spray rate of the ethylcellullose dispersion are the two most important variables that control the drug release rate from the coated tablets and the microindentations hardness of the untreated coat.
the three process variables studied have a significant effect on the performance of the polymeric coat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inlet-air temperature is the most critical coating process variable in the case of the Surelease dispersion and that the drug release rate from the coated tablets could be controlled by manipulating the inlet-air temperature and the spray rate of the dispersion during coating.

Surelease is a useful coating polymer for controlled release of drugs from the coated tablets, and that the response surface methodology is a useful tool for the optimization of process variables in fluid-bed coating.
the 3-D response surfaces generated using RSM provide useful information on the complex interrelationships among the coating process variables, and the drug release rate from the coated tablets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the complex relationship between coating process variables and the performance characteristics of coated tablets is possible through the use of response surface methodology.
the inlet-air temperature plays an important role in controlling the rate of drug release and the hardness of the coat applied.
RSM can be used as an effective tool to study the effect of selected independent coating process parameters on selected response variables.
